modalLead: Sharing reaches the health view, and the share entry now tells the truth about what your browser will do with it — including on Safari, which offers Web Share over plain http:// and then refuses every call.

items.text: Copy URL and Share in the health view — a row there is a bookmark like any other, but copying or sending one used to mean finding it again on the dashboard first. Both entries now sit in the per-row More menu, between Find in Web Archive and Change checking. Neither is a repair, so they appear on every row, healthy or broken.

The entry no longer promises a share sheet that cannot open — Safari on macOS refuses sharing over plain http://, localhost included, while still reporting the feature as available. Checking only whether the browser has sharing was therefore not enough: the menu offered Share…, nothing appeared, and the link was quietly copied instead. A refusal is now remembered — the link is still copied, the message explains that this browser will not open a sheet here, and the entry re-labels itself to Copy name + URL rather than repeating a promise it has already broken.

For a real share sheet, reach the dashboard over HTTPS — through a reverse proxy or a tunnel such as Tailscale. Chrome and Firefox on macOS and Linux have no Web Share at all, at any address, and there the entry simply reads Copy name + URL from the start.

Copy URL and Copy name + URL sit next to each other — where no sheet can open, the two entries are adjacent, which makes the difference between them visible: one is the link, the other the title and the link.
